detail.abstract:
Background: U.S. critical infrastructure depends on deep, multi-tier supply networks whose failures propagate across sectors, yet federal risk management for these networks remains largely periodic and retrospective. Machine learning has been applied to supplier-level disruption prediction and network economics has documented how shocks propagate, but little work evaluates, under an explicit false-alert cost, whether early-warning systems that exploit supply-network structure give critical-service operators more lead time than monitoring of immediate suppliers.
Objective: To develop a conceptual framework for AI-enabled early detection of supply chain failure in critical infrastructure, to state it as four testable propositions, and to examine those propositions in a transparent, fully synthetic proof-of-concept.
Methods: We synthesized peer-reviewed literature and U.S. policy documents (1997-2026) on supply chain resilience, production-network propagation, machine-learning disruption prediction, anomaly detection, and critical infrastructure policy. We then built a fictional five-tier, four-sector, 120-node dependency network (KIRC) with simulated weekly signals, disruption events with precursors, and lagged propagation, and compared five detectors at matched false-alert budgets across 40 replicate synthetic worlds: a tier-1 threshold monitor (A), a multi-tier Isolation Forest (B), a propagation-aware graph detector (C), and two supervised gradient-boosting detectors trained on separate labeled worlds (D1 without and D2 with graph-exposure features). Sensitivity analyses varied noise, cross-sector coupling, event frequency, dependency-map completeness, visibility depth, link delays, precursor length, the propagation rule, and signal withholding and injection; thresholds were also set from held-out calibration worlds.
Results: In the synthetic worlds, the graph detector discriminated impending critical-node failures better than the tier-1 monitor (AUC 0.75 versus 0.59; paired difference +0.158, 95% bootstrap interval 0.150 to 0.166, in all 40 worlds). At a budget of ten false-alert episodes per world, event-level recall was 0.31 for C and 0.31 for B versus 0.21 for A, and mean warning lead time was 1.27, 1.31 and 0.89 weeks; the paired differences between C and B on these metrics included zero. Most failure onsets went unwarned by every unsupervised detector (69-79%). The discrimination advantage of C narrowed from +0.15 to +0.05 AUC with 40% of dependency edges missing and to +0.02 with 60% missing, and did not grow with cross-sector coupling. The supervised detectors warned far more: recall 0.68 (D1) and 0.89 (D2) with mean lead times of 3.0 and 6.6 weeks, and graph-exposure features added to supervised performance (D2 over D1: +0.21 recall, +3.6 weeks); but they were trained on worlds generated by the same process as the test worlds. Fixed thresholds from held-out worlds changed conclusions little. Because propagation and precursors were built into the data-generating process, all results are illustrative only.
Conclusions: The framework identifies multi-tier visibility, dependency-map completeness, labeled incident history, and false-alert budgeting as the design choices on which early-warning value depends, and it yields falsifiable propositions for testing against real supplier, logistics, and infrastructure data. The proof-of-concept offers no evidence that any real system would perform as simulated; it demonstrates the logic, the evaluation protocol, and the conditions under which the expected advantage erodes.

detail.abstract: Many people assume that the World to Come belongs mainly to great Torah scholars and that ordinary people can at best hope for a modest place behind them. Rabbinic literature places enormous value on Torah study, but it also tells a different story. This paper examines stories from the Babylonian Talmud, the Jerusalem Talmud, and the Midrash in which Heaven singles out people with no claim to learning. They include a repentant sinner, two Roman officials, an executioner, a prison guard, two jesters, a bloodletter, a launderer, a donkey driver, a brothel keeper, a woodcutter, a repentant apostate, two butchers, a schoolteacher, and the wife of a great sage. Some earn their reward through a single act of courage or repentance. Others earn it through years of quiet kindness, such as caring for aging parents or making sure the poor are not shamed. Again and again, a great sage is surprised and learns that Heaven does not measure people the way scholars do. The rabbis who told these stories were scholars themselves, and they told them as a warning against the pride that learning can bring. The paper concludes that these stories hold a lesson for today's academics, who can easily confuse education with wisdom or goodness and look down on the people they should be learning from.

title: Who Cares for the Caregivers?

detail.abstract: This article examines the role of elderly Black women and other women of color as caregivers and nurses, and the resulting lack of access many face to long-term health care and meaningful bargaining power. detail.abstract: AI agents look 10 to 150 times cheaper than human workers per task, but much of that gap comes from costs AI does not pay and risks it does not carry. This paper sets out the structural cost differences between human and AI labour. It identifies five inputs that humans pay for and AI largely does not: knowledge acquisition, social obligations (tax, superannuation, insurance), liability, externalities, and the cost of undetected error. We propose a risk-adjusted cost model: work cost, plus review cost, plus the cost of redoing failed tasks, plus error probability times error loss, plus compliance. We embed it in a two-producer, two-task model of comparative advantage and production possibility frontiers and calibrate it for four Australian occupations, labelling every input by evidence strength. Three findings stand out. First, error risk can reverse comparative advantage: ignoring error losses, AI looks comparatively better at legal work than routine contact-centre work, but once expected error losses are counted humans hold the comparative advantage in judgment. Second, the cheapest arrangement saves only 14-68% per task against a human alone, far below headline ratios of 9x-66x, and the rankings are most sensitive to human error rates and agent success rates. Third, private and social costs diverge: medical liability prices a diagnostic error at about A$6, far below its harm, so private calculations undervalue accuracy. A hybrid worker using AI as a tool is cheapest only where AI strongly lifts that person's output, mainly for less experienced workers. On the output side, AI output adds less to local incomes, often cannot be owned, and may degrade the human knowledge supply it is trained on. Whether unpriced inputs inflate AI's measured advantage is framed as a hypothesis to quantify. We discuss policy options, separating transfers from real costs: Australia's decision to rule out a text-and-data-mining exception and the licensing models still under consultation, collective licensing, levies, transparency rules, liability rules and professional regulation.

detail.abstract: Asset-pricing theory predicts low risk premia in good times. We test this prediction with a physical measure of real activity: the carbon dioxide U.S. industry emits as it burns fuel. When industry runs hot, expected returns are low. A one-standard-deviation increase in emissions predicts a 4.2 percentage point lower market excess return over the next year. Emissions forecast returns out of sample up to five years ahead; at one year, their forecasts encompass those of 20 established predictors. Return decompositions trace the predictability to discount rates, not cash flows. Industry's carbon footprint thus tracks the price of risk.

detail.abstract:
There is a popular Latin maxim which states "interesse rei publicae ut sit finis litium," meaning it is in the public interest that there be an end to litigation. However, this does not adequately reflect the post-judgment situation in Nigeria. The assumption of an ordinary Nigerian would be that once a debtor has defaulted, been sued and judgment obtained against him, that marks the end of litigation with regard to recovery of the debt in question. But the question that leaves begging an answer is: what happens when a defaulting party decides not to adhere to the judgment of court? This is where the law has devised means through which the person owed the debt may enforce the judgment.

This paper therefore focuses on one of the most profound means of debt recovery in Nigeria - garnishee proceedings. Although this is an already well-explored area of legal discourse, a peculiar area has raised controversy in the conduct of these proceedings, specifically where government funds are involved. This paper aims to expatiate on the now-settled judicial position on this controversy, through judicial insight from a recent Nigerian Supreme Court decision. In doing so, it commences by examining the meaning, nature, and peculiarities of garnishee proceedings in Nigeria, followed by an analysis of section 84 of the Sheriffs and Civil Process Act, 2004. A comparison is then drawn between two cases on the subject matter in which Nigerian courts reached opposing conclusions, giving rise to the controversy referenced above. To this effect, an analysis of the Supreme Court's decision in C.B.N. v. Lidan Engineering (2026) is conducted, and its resultant effect on section 84 is examined

detail.abstract: We document that the effect of mandatory emissions disclosure policies is highly heterogeneous and depends on firms' financial strength. Using a difference in differences framework and firm level data from the US, we examine the impact of the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program. The results indicate that energy firms translate disclosure pressure into operational restructuring leading to a reduction in emissions of around 34 percentage. The decline in costs remains larger than the decline in sales, and gross margins increase by 3.5 to 6.6 percentage points relative to reportable non-energy firms. This effect is however concentrated in firms that were financially sound and had higher institutional ownership. Improvements in performance in the full sample are mainly driven by financially stronger energy firms. This suggests that mandatory disclosure is not a universally effective policy tool.

detail.abstract: Private credit raises a supervisory question rather than a presumption of systemic fragility: under what observable conditions can losses in predominantly non-bank corporate lending reach banks and the wider supply of credit? This article develops a layered framework that separates direct portfolio impairment, contingent bank liquidity demand and net bank credit loss, and quantifies each layer with transparent, reproducible tools. Using the Financial Stability Board's end-2024 private-credit asset range of US$1.5-2.0 trillion as an exposure base, author-selected three-year scenarios imply direct portfolio losses of US$27-36 billion, US$90-120 billion and US$206-275 billion. Three results follow. First, the scenarios map closely onto observed default evidence: the severe scenario corresponds to the persistence for three years of the default rate already reported in one monitored subpopulation, and a multi-period single-factor credit model places it at roughly the 94th percentile of the base-case loss distribution rather than in a remote tail. Second, a fund-level waterfall shows that, with the equity cushions documented in recent fund-level evidence and the leverage ceilings of current EU and US regimes, even the severe scenario does not reach senior bank facilities unless losses are concentrated in small or thinly capitalised vehicles. Third, the binding transmission risks therefore lie where public data are weakest: concentrated vehicles, facility-level lending, common borrowers, undrawn commitments and the concentration of bank exposure in a few institutions. The article translates these results into a proportionate supervisory dataset built on common borrower and facility identifiers, risk-sensitive reporting frequencies and a claim-allocation protocol that prevents double counting.

detail.abstract: Firms cut hours or duties when demand stays weak and restore them when it recovers, while long term contracts insure pay. We study the joint design of workload and pay when the firm commits to a contract but the worker can quit at any time. A market state drives revenue under a high and a low workload, and switching is costly both ways. With an outside option common to both workloads, we characterize the optimal policy for every resumption cost. Under each workload, pay follows a predetermined path and rises only when the outside option binds. First, the workload should respond to pay relative to the market state, so the market levels that trigger a switch must be revised whenever pay or the workload changes. When resumptions do not coincide with a binding outside option, the thresholds are exactly those of a firm that could bind the worker to stay. In our examples, the best rules we found with market levels fixed over the whole contract lose over a third of the gain from using both workloads. Second, the right to quit can make a temporary reduction permanent, because the floor under pay lets compensation for lost leisure absorb part of the revenue gain from a resumption. Third, at intermediate resumption costs the firm restores the workload exactly when the outside option binds and makes an additional upward pay adjustment beyond the pay difference between the workloads.

detail.abstract: How does bank maturity transformation create priced systemic risk in the cross section of asset returns? We develop an intertemporal asset pricing model (Liquidity ICAPM) in which systemic liquidity risk arises endogenously from banks' joint choices of short-term debt dependence and illiquid asset exposure. Because runnable funding and asset illiquidity are structural complements, aggregate fragility takes a multiplicative form that forecasts investment opportunities and enters the stochastic discount factor. Monetary policy tightening lowers new maturity mismatch only when asset-side contraction dominates deposit-spread expansion, while simultaneously inflicting valuation losses on legacy assets. In equilibrium, the price of systemic liquidity risk is countercyclical, financial leverage amplifies asset liquidity betas, and liquidity regulation mitigates fragility. Across U.S. commercial banks and REITs from 1994 to 2024, portfolio sorts and Fama-MacBeth regressions show that high liquidity-beta assets underperform low-beta peers by 6% to 17% per quarter during systemic stress, confirming a significant negative stress-state price of liquidity risk.

detail.abstract: Market participants frequently engage in what practitioners colloquially call 'vibe-based accounting,' relying on intuition and narrative rather than fundamentals. However, the academic literature lacks a unified reduced-form model to explain why identical rhetorical strategies and resource expenditures yield vastly different market outcomes. This paper introduces a signed-credibility framework. I argue that credibility is not a binary state but a signed real variable (C ∈ ℝ). When credibility is positive, rhetoric acts as a self-fulfilling prophecy and resources are optional. When credibility is negative, rhetoric backfires, and resource expenditure acts as a cost that accelerates market losses. I formalize this dynamic into a single reduced-form equation incorporating institutional capacity, market reflexivity, and resource adequacy. The model is tested against three historical case studies: the ECB's 2012 'Whatever it takes' pledge, the 1992 Black Wednesday crisis, and recent U.S. Treasury interventions. The framework successfully predicts market 1 outcomes where traditional reserve-based crisis models fall short.

detail.abstract: Islamic venture capital and private equity require an account of how investment contracts, managerial authority, remuneration and investor protection operate together. This paper develops an integrated jurisprudential framework for examining those relationships within Malaysia's capitalmarket regime. A qualitative doctrinal analysis combines selected contemporary scholarship, statutory provisions, regulatory guidance and contractual standards with an explicitly conditional application of fiqh and uṣūl al-fiqh. Ten components are selected through the fund lifecycle: the manager, investors, investment committee, advisory committee, management fees, carried interest, board representation, protective rights, exits and termination. The analysis identifies three distinctions essential to coherent structuring: the fund's legal vehicle differs from its Sharīʿah contract; internal governance does not necessarily create a separate agency; and investor consent does not remove mandatory legal or Sharīʿah constraints. Malaysia already provides a dedicated registration regime and specific Islamic VC/PE requirements, including flexibility in screening unlisted investments. The remaining issue examined here is how those requirements translate into consistent fund documentation. Muḍārabah, fee-based investment agency and carefully separated composite arrangements are evaluated as alternatives, rather than treating a hybrid as universally necessary. A hypothetical fund example illustrates the framework's application to remuneration, conflicts and loss allocation. The contribution is a structured method for identifying and resolving contractual inconsistencies; transaction-level approval and empirical validation remain necessary.

title: A Learning-Based System for Automatic Table Tennis Stroke Assessment Using a Racket-Mounted Inertial Measurement Unit

detail.title: A Learning-Based System for Automatic Table Tennis Stroke Assessment Using a Racket-Mounted Inertial Measurement Unit
detail.abstract: Accurate stroke assessment is essential for table tennis coaching. Traditional methods rely on expert observation or expensive motion-capture systems, which are impractical for daily training. As an alternative, researchers use an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) attached to the table tennis racket to measure movement parameters, combined with a learning system. This study presents an automatic stroke assessment system that classifies forehand stroke types (basic, topspin, and push), evaluates player skill level (professional and novice), and scores technique quality (on a 100-point scale) using a single racket-mounted IMU and machine learning models. This study involved 16 players (8 professionals, 8 novices) who performed the three stroke types. Five learning-based models were compared: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN), a CNN-LSTM hybrid, Random Forest (RF), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). For stroke recognition, all models performed well (94–97% accuracy), with LSTM achieving the best result (97%). For skill classification, performance dropped substantially (66–75% accuracy), reflecting the difficulty of distinguishing skill levels from a single stroke; LSTM again performed best (75%). For technique quality assessment, ensemble methods outperformed deep learning models. Random Forest achieved the best Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 7.43 and an R-squared (R²) of 0.742, while XGBoost achieved the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 2.79. These findings reveal that model suitability is task-dependent: LSTM excels at classification tasks, whereas ensemble methods are more effective for regression-based quality estimation. This study provides practical guidance for designing wearable, learning-driven coaching systems using minimal sensing configurations.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the strategic behavior and market impact of deep reinforcement learning (RL) agents operating within a high-frequency continuous double auction limit order book (LOB) environment. Utilizing a multi-agent framework governed by Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), we examine how autonomous trading agents learn optimal execution, quoting, and inventory management strategies under varying degrees of market friction and order flow toxicity. Our findings indicate that RL agents naturally discover canonical market-making behaviors, widening spreads under high inventory risk and engaging in predatory order-spoofing during high-volatility regimes. Furthermore, we analyze the permanent and temporary price impact generated by agent execution policies, demonstrating that RL-driven strategies significantly minimize implementation shortfalls relative to static benchmark execution algorithms (TWAP and VWAP).

detail.abstract: This article argues that official gold holdings should be treated as a third pillar of taka stabilization, alongside interest-rate policy and exchange-rate flexibility. The motivation is Bangladesh’s post-2021 reserve depletion, the exchange-rate adjustments of 2024–25, the IMF-supported shift toward a more flexible exchange-rate regime, and the country’s unusually concentrated export base. The study synthesizes primary evidence from IMF, World Bank, Asian Development Bank, Bangladesh Bank, and World Gold Council sources. It combines a literature-based interpretation of cross-country panel evidence, a Bangladeshspecific event chronology, and an original scenario analysis of gold-accumulation paths for Bangladesh Bank. Three findings emerge. First, active diversification into gold over the past two decades has been led by emerging markets; reserve managers value gold most during economic, financial, and geopolitical stress, and higher central-bank gold holdings are associated with lower sovereign credit default swap spreads, particularly during crises. Second, the May 2024 step adjustment and the May 2025 crawling peg moderated reserve losses without immediately restoring adequacy — IMF staff assessed reserve cover at roughly 3.6 months in late 2025 against a safe threshold near 4.9 months — but Bangladesh Bank data show reserves recovering to US$32.9 billion on the BPM6 basis by end-FY2026, satisfying the trigger conditions this article sets for a strategic build. Third, scenario arithmetic shows that raising official holdings from 14.28 tonnes to 20–25 tonnes is affordable now, that 35–50 tonnes is defensible only conditionally, and that 75 tonnes would imply a very large composition shift. The article therefore proposes a sequenced, rule-bound accumulation strategy governed by an explicit liquid-asset floor, a prohibition on debt-financed purchases, quarterly disclosure, and internationally recognized custody. Gold complements rather than substitutes for orthodox stabilization: it improves reserve quality only where transparent rules and market-based exchange-rate adjustment accompany it.

detail.abstract:
Background: In 2026, Brazil marks the 30th anniversary of the Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC), a major non-contributory social pension programme supporting older adults and persons with disabilities. We evaluated its health and economic effects over three decades and projected outcomes to 2030.

Methods: We used fixed-effects Poisson models to assess associations between BPC coverage and health outcomes across 5,570 Brazilian municipalities (hospitalisations and mortality) and 27 states (YLLs, YLDs and DALYs). Retrospective analyses were complemented by sensitivity analyses, counterfactual simulations, economic evaluation and projections to 2030.

Findings: Each one-percentage-point increase in BPC coverage was associated with reductions of 2.9% in hospitalisations, 0.6% in mortality and 3.9% in DALYs. The programme was estimated to have averted 13.0 million hospitalisations and 571,019 deaths over 1996–2025, and 69.6 million DALYs over 1996–2023. The incremental cost was US$2,738 per DALY averted (95% UI: US$2,056–4,068), equivalent to 35.3% of Brazil's average GDP per capita. Monetised mortality benefits were 3.81 times incremental BPC expenditure (95% UI: 2.57–5.07). Expanding eligibility was projected to avert an additional 2.55 million hospitalisations, 43,731 deaths and 12.61 million DALYs (95% UI: 0.42–21.99 million) over 2026–2030.

Interpretation: Higher BPC coverage was associated with substantial population health gains in Brazil over three decades, with the economic value of reduced mortality exceeding incremental programme expenditure nearly fourfold. Expanding coverage could yield further health gains by 2030, whereas restricting eligibility could reverse some gains. These findings underscore the importance of weighing health benefits against fiscal costs in NCSP assessments, highlighting its role in advancing health equity, the Sustainable Development Goals, and leaving no one behind.

detail.abstract: This paper extends break-even analysis with uncertainty and managerial flexibility for small firms. Put-call parity equates the value of full cost flexibility with expected loss; partial avoidability makes it vanish quickly. A volatility estimator needs only the best and worst period, and the framework is translated into plain-language indicators for owners: the margin of safety, the probability of a loss-making month, and a reserve sized to the expected shortfall. Descriptive IRS and Kauffman Firm Survey data on far smaller businesses show that losses are common and that cost structures differ widely across industries, but they cannot calibrate the framework, which is best used to communicate exposure.

detail.abstract: Correct identification of pure sorghum seed varieties is important for breeding and seed production, but the traditional methods employed require specialized skills not available to all stakeholders in the seed value chain, especially in Botswana. Deep learning using convolutional neural networks (CNN) is a new approach to seed classification which is potentially more accurate and accessible than the traditional methods. Therefore, seven CNN models were assessed for possible deployment in a mobile computing platform as a base model for accurate and automatic classification of three sorghum seed varieties from Botswana. The effect of topological depth and network design on classification performance was investigated using the following CNN models of topological depths ranging from seven to 389 layers: AlexNet, VGG16, Xception, MobileNetV2, InceptionV3, DenseNet121, and NASNetMobile. In addition, model size was taken into consideration as a factor influencing portability. Results showed that the models with lower topological depths performed better than the ones with higher depths, with test losses and accuracies, respectively, ranging from 0.17 to 0.77 and 0.67 to 0.94. Correspondingly, Precision, Recall and F1-scores ranged between 0.67 and 0.94 across all models evaluated. However, the networks of lower topology produced very large models, while the ones with higher topological depths produced smaller sized models. In conclusion, the DenseNet121 model is recommended for optimization for deployment as a base model for a mobile sorghum seed classification system owing to its good prediction performance (accuracy and F1 score of 0.8), and its lean size of only 54.9MB and 10,146,891 parameters.

detail.abstract: Based on a sample of 28 sub-Saharan African countries from 2005 to 2020, this paper investigates the relationship between financial development, economic growth and governance in countries. By applying panel data econometrics through fixed effects (Hausman test), we mainly highlight a negative and significant interaction effect between economic growth and governance in the countries as perceived by fundamental rights and freedoms on the one hand, and the quality of public administration and finances on the other. This result leads us to consider economic growth as a moderator in the relationship between good governance in countries and the development of their financial systems.

detail.abstract: We study how poor domestic transport infrastructure shapes the distributional effects of integration with world markets. Exploiting India's large-scale trade liberalization in the 1990s, together with a digitized road network, we find that reductions in input tariffs generate substantially larger manufacturing gains in districts with better access to international ports, accompanied by faster reallocation of workers out of agriculture and into manufacturing and producer services, and greater migration from more remote regions. We interpret these findings through a quantitative spatial model. A key mechanism is that manufacturing intermediates are more time-sensitive in transit than manufacturing output, leading to larger increases in the relative returns to manufacturing in districts with better port access. The model replicates our main empirical findings and reveals stark distributional inequalities from liberalization, with gains in real income, real wages, and real rents heavily skewed toward regions with better port access. Finally, a simultaneous highway expansion targeted at improving port connectivity eliminates these spatial inequalities in welfare gains while generating net aggregate benefits.

detail.abstract: Informal transport gig workers experience irregular earnings, variable operating costs, vehicle-related risks, and uneven access to conventional social protection. This paper develops a crosscountry econometric framework for examining whether uptake of on-demand microinsurance is associated with a lower probability of emergency asset liquidation after a financial shock. It integrates worker characteristics, telematics indicators, mobile-money activity, cash-flow volatility, emergency savings, and access to formal credit. The illustrative analysis uses 1,500 programmatically generated worker records, divided equally across the United States, Ghana, and Kenya. Probit models are specified for insurance uptake and asset liquidation, while nearest-neighbour propensity-score matching is used to demonstrate adjustment for observed selection differences. In the synthetic sample, insurance uptake is 57.1%, financial shocks affect 35.5% of records, and emergency asset liquidation occurs in 19.0%. Liquidation is 16.7% among insured records and 22.0% among uninsured records; the unadjusted difference is-5.3 percentage points and the matched contrast is approximately-4.0 percentage points. These values are outputs of the simulation and are not estimates from actual workers or evidence of a causal insurance effect. The paper contributes a reproducible research design, clarifies identification requirements, and outlines data-governance safeguards for future empirical work. The analysis emphasises that uptake, coverage adequacy, claims eligibility, and financial resilience are distinct concepts. Telematics and mobile-money data may improve measurement of exposure and payment behaviour, but they may also introduce selection, privacy, and fairness concerns. The proposed framework therefore treats digital traces as imperfect indicators rather than comprehensive representations of workers' financial lives. It recommends a longitudinal observed-data design with explicit product definitions, pre-treatment covariates, balance diagnostics, common-support checks, sensitivity analysis, and country-specific institutional documentation before policy conclusions are drawn.

detail.abstract: The institutional matrix that exists within a country usually has considerable impact on production and transaction costs within the national economy. Considering the insecurity crisis linked to terrorism affecting the Sahel countries, marked by "coups d'Etat" and terrorist actions in certain nations (Burkina Faso, Guinea-Conakry, Mali, Niger, Chad), this article retrospectively mobilizes neo-institutional theory to analyze the behavior of debt maturity for companies listed on the BRVM during the periods of civil war and post-electoral crisis in Côte d'Ivoire (2005, 2006, 2007, 2010 and 2011). Using a multicounty sample of 207 firm-year observations, over the period 2005-2014, drawn from listed companies in the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) Regional Securities Exchange, we find the following evidence. First, debt maturity is longer with better quality of country policy and institutional assessment (CPIA) and a higher annual growth rate in gross domestic product (GDP). Second, we find a negative and statistically significant association between debt maturity and foreign direct investment flows, leading firms to borrow at short intervals. Third, we observe a negative and significant effect of country policy and institutional assessment on debt maturity, during periods of political instability. In addition, the results show that annual growth rate in GDP is lower during periods of political instability compared to periods of relative political stability. Lastly, we find that foreign direct investment flows are positive and significantly associated with debt maturity, leading firms to prefer borrowing for long periods of time.

affiliations.org_name: University of Birmingham - Birmingham Law School
affiliations.preferred_name: University of Birmingham - Birmingham Law School

detail.abstract: Groundwater is a largely unseen common pool resource. Yet, driven by strong economic incentives, whether or not encouraged by existing policies, and the difficulty to exclude others, groundwater users are competing with each other to extract as much as possible, with devastating consequences for its sustainability. The challenges faced for sustainably managing such common pool resources, on which people have established de facto individual rights, are manifold. However, creating a market for trades of some kind in ecosystem services associated with groundwater could actually enhance the protection of this critical resource on the basis that protection can benefit individual groundwater users economically as well as provide a broader public good. This article uses Elinor Ostrom's design principles as an analytical tool to examine how market-based approaches such as payments for ecosystem services (PES) fit with some of the governance models that could be used to protect and enhance groundwater as a common pool resource. It argues that while there are specific design challenges to be overcome, PES as an institutional tool can align with Ostrom's ideas for the governance of groundwater.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the location determinants of foreign direct investment (FDI) across Indonesia's provinces and updates the provincial inward FDI attractiveness index. It uses a new balanced panel of 33 provinces at 2010 boundaries for 2010-2024, built from official investment-realisation (LKPM) microdata, BPS regional accounts by expenditure, Susenas illiteracy rates and a set of policy indicators. Unlike the original version of this study, which relied on random effects, the models are estimated with province and year fixed effects. Hausman and Mundlak tests reject random effects in favour of fixed effects. Within provinces, lagged market size is the most robust determinant across estimators, standarderror corrections and a wild-cluster bootstrap. A fall in net exports relative to output, which signals import-intensive absorption, precedes higher FDI, and lower adult illiteracy is associated with more FDI under some error structures. Accumulated FDI attracts further manufacturing and services FDI. Efficiency wages, human development and conflict show no within-province effect: their influence works through permanent differences between provinces. The fixed-effects design is used to estimate the effects of several policy dummy variables. Operational Special Economic Zones (KEK) have no measurable effect on provincial FDI, a result that holds under estimators robust to staggered adoption. The nickel ore export ban sharply increased basic-metals FDI in the three nickel provinces. The Omnibus Law and risk-based licensing did not favour provinces outside Java. The attractiveness index shows that Java still ranks highest on fundamentals, with Jakarta the most attractive province, while the nickel provinces have become high-performing enclaves. Indonesia's FDI has become less concentrated in Java mainly because of commodity-specific industrial policy, not broad-based improvements in location advantages.

detail.abstract: Fifty years after Rosen (1974), applied hedonic practice still rests on a series of specification choices-functional form, temporal controls, spatial controls, estimation method-that are usually made by convention and rarely stress-tested jointly. Using 514,212 Quebec residential sales (2021-2026) whose structural descriptors come from the provincial assessment roll, we run a controlled horse race of twenty hedonic models organised along those four axes, scoring every model on identical holdouts and on the same price-level scoreboard (log models are Duan-retransformed, Box-Cox inverted). Four lessons emerge. (1) Functional form is a second-order choice: from linear to splines, the median absolute error spans 16.5-18.6%, and the data-driven Box-Cox exponent (λ = 0.25) buys nothing out of sample. (2) Controls are first-order: dropping spatial fixed effects costs ten error points-location granularity matters far more than curvature, but only up to the point where cells thin out (a ∼1 km grid overfits). (3) Under random validation, estimation method matters most: gradient boosting reaches 14.4%-a 13% improvement over the best linear model-with random forests close behind, and coordinates alone reproduce what thousands of dummies buy. (4) But the ranking is an artifact of the split: under a forward-in-time holdout (train < 2025, test 2025-26) every model degrades and the machine-learning advantage reverses-the spline hedonic posts a lower median error than gradient boosting and an identical log-scale R 2-a stark warning against evaluating valuation models with random cross-validation alone. Constant-quality monthly indices implied by the competing forms agree to within a few index points, and the boosted model's implicit age and floor-area profiles track the quadratic OLS closely-interpretation and prediction disagree less than the random-validation gap suggests.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the information content embedded in equity option markets for predicting returns and realized volatility across multiple asset classes and market regimes. Using 3.83 billion option contracts on 11,077 underlyings (2010-2025) merged with 11.5 billion intraday OHLCV observations across stocks, ETFs, indices, futures, FX, and cryptocurrencies, I address five research questions. Option-implied moments-particularly implied kurtosis, skewness, and put-call ratiossignificantly predict 5-day stock returns; quintile long-short portfolios sorted on implied kurtosis deliver annualized Sharpe ratios of 2.33 (𝑡 = 19.84). Augmenting the HAR-RV model with implied volatility surface features improves 1-day realized variance forecasting by 23.3% in 𝑅 2 (0.359 to 0.442), an improvement robust across all subperiods including COVID-19 (+19.4%). The ratio of implied to realized correlation among S&P 500 constituents predicts market stress at 5, 10, and 20-day horizons (𝑡-statistics: 3.91-8.30). Granger causality confirms that ATM implied volatility leads realized volatility in 100% of individual tickers (𝐹 = 62.4), and variance decomposition shows IV shocks explain 73.8% of RV forecast error variance at the 20-day horizon. All findings survive Newey-West HAC (up to 22 lags), double-clustered standard errors, subperiod and leave-one-yearout analysis, VIX-regime conditioning, quantile regressions, winsorization sensitivity, rank-based information coefficients, decile sorts, and a within-ticker permutation placebo.

detail.abstract: We study optimal consumption and investment when the consumption equivalent of remaining lifetime utility must stay above a fixed fraction of its historical maximum. The guarantee protects the value of the remaining consumption plan while leaving current spending free to adjust. We formulate the problem as the minimum cost of delivering a prescribed continuation utility. In utility flow coordinates the path constraints are linear, and for power utility a Legendre transform reduces the funding equation to a linear Euler equation whose free boundaries solve scalar equations. Depending on the discount rate and the protection level, the utility record either grows at the upper boundary or never moves. We prove existence and uniqueness in both regimes, construct the optimal consumption and portfolio through a doubly reflected diffusion, and verify optimality on the infinite horizon for relative risk aversion below and above one, including singular boundaries. The optimal plan also solves a proportional wealth drawdown problem whose ratio is a strictly increasing function of the protected fraction and always exceeds it. For positive utility flows, a convex formulation yields existence and convergence of finite constraint relaxations. Numerical examples quantify the funding premium and the implied wealth drawdown.

title: Does the Sales Comparison Approach Actually Work? A Large-Scale Point-in-Time Validation of Comparable Selection, Price Adjustments, and Value Reconciliation

detail.title: Does the Sales Comparison Approach Actually Work? A Large-Scale Point-in-Time Validation of Comparable Selection, Price Adjustments, and Value Reconciliation

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study uses secondary real estate transaction and municipal property assessment data from Quebec, Canada, covering the period 2021–2026. The analysis focuses on transaction prices, property characteristics, geographic attributes, comparable-sales selection, and valuation model performance. No human participants were recruited, and no experimental interventions were conducted. The research consists of retrospective statistical and econometric analyses of property-level records.

detail.abstract: The sales comparison approach is the dominant method of residential valuation, yet its operating rules-how many comparables to use, how far and how far back to search, which adjustments to apply, how to weight and reconcile-rest largely on professional convention. We subject these rules to a large-scale, point-in-time backtest on 390,996 arm's-length single-family transactions in Quebec (2021-2026) matched to the municipal assessment roll. For each of 189,354 target sales in 2024-2026, the price is masked and 2,256 configurations of the approach-together with hedonic, gradient-boosting, assessment-ratio and hybrid benchmarks-are applied using only information available on the valuation date; configurations are selected on 2024 and evaluated out of sample on 2025-2026. Adjustments dominate: the median absolute error of the five nearest sales falls from 18.1% with a time adjustment only to 13.0% with a hedonic adjustment grid, and a stylized conventional grid captures most of that gain. Selecting physically similar rather than merely nearby comparables delivers a comparable gain without any adjustment. The optimal number of comparables is well above the conventional three-around twenty once a grid is applied, with no penalty up to fifty-and short time windows are dominated; the search radius matters far less than the number and similarity of the sales retained. Weighting and reconciliation rules matter little. The best transparent configuration chosen in 2024 reaches 11.1% out of sample, against 9.0% for a quarterly-retrained gradient-boosting model that uses the assessed value and 8.9% for a hybrid; the cost of transparency is small and narrows in homogeneous submarkets. Accuracy is governed primarily by submarket liquidity; a wide-net rule that retains the most similar sales is self-adapting, and stratum-specific rules do not improve on it. The results turn a convention-based method into a set of empirically validated, reproducible rules.

title: Narrative Intelligence: Fiction as an Instrument of Strategic Inquiry

detail.title: Narrative Intelligence: Fiction as an Instrument of Strategic Inquiry

detail.abstract:
Technological innovation changes what states and institutions can do, but rarely determines
how they will behave when a new capability reaches the point of decision. Intelligence organisations
routinely examine futures for which decisive evidence does not yet exist. They can establish
capabilities and dependencies, but must also ask how actors possessing unequal information,
authority and obligations could turn those conditions into unforeseen outcomes. Fiction is already
used for this purpose in strategic foresight, science-fiction prototyping and fictional intelligence. The
neglected question is not whether stories can depict possible futures, but what the act of composing
an inhabited fictional situation adds to inquiry and what evidential standing its conclusions possess.
This article develops a bounded account of narrative composition as strategic inquiry: writing an
evidence-constrained scene obliges the author to specify what actors know, decide and experience as
a technological or institutional system changes around them. Such composition can yield candidate
how-possibly explanations, not estimates of likelihood. It proposes a contemporaneous composition
record separating assumptions held before drafting from questions exposed or revised during
drafting. Drawing on the philosophy of models, counterfactual reasoning and cognitive research on
narrative, it distinguishes fictional coherence from support for a real causal mechanism, and makes
explicit the risks of hindsight, false empathy and probability inflation. Its contribution is a proposed
discipline of traceable composition and conditional explanation, directed particularly at the gap
between technological capability and institutional adaptation.

detail.title: Recursive Representation Equilibrium: Persistence, Invisible Fragility, and Reflexive Stability of Capital-Carried Information Architectures

detail.abstract: Recursive Representation Equilibrium (RRE) studies financial markets in which a predictive representation selected today becomes part of the capital state from which the next allocation problem is solved. RRE recovers contemporaneous Representation Equilibrium exactly as its one-period restriction and separates current market clearing from recursive state reproduction. In a capacity-preserving economy, persistence requires both recursive incentive compatibility and reproduction of the incumbent representation-capital distribution. Under linear clearing, the premium observes this state only through an aggregate exposure map. We show constructively that two allocations can have the same aggregate exposure, clearing premium, established position, and maintained Gaussian screening-off certificates while differing in recursive persistence, even when the persistent allocation is optimal against a continuous certified representation menu. We call this invisible fragility. On regular local RRE branches, the state-transition derivative decomposes into direct and price-mediated feedback. Price-blind reallocations can therefore remain dynamically active, and stationary RRE states with the same premium can have different local stability. The results distinguish contemporaneous clearing, recursive persistence, price identification, and local equilibrium stability.

title: The Effect of Interest Rate Changes on Bank Profitability and Credit Growth: The Decoupling of Price and Quantity Instruments in Türkiye (2021-2026)

detail.title: The Effect of Interest Rate Changes on Bank Profitability and Credit Growth: The Decoupling of Price and Quantity Instruments in Türkiye (2021-2026)

detail.abstract: This paper examines the effect of the policy rate on bank profitability and credit growth in Türkiye over 2021-2026, placing at its centre the relationship between the price instrument of monetary policy (the policy rate) and its quantity instruments (reserve requirements tied to credit growth). The period constitutes an unusual natural experiment, spanning three distinct policy regimes: deeply negative real-rate easing (2021-mid-2023), rapid high-amplitude tightening (mid-2023-2024), and a prolonged plateau of constant rates following gradual normalisation (2025-2026). Using indicators derived from published aggregate data of the BRSA, the CBRT, TurkStat and the Banks Association of Türkiye, three findings emerge. First, the gap between nominal and real profitability is systematic: sector return on equity has remained below inflation without interruption since 2020, recovering to -2.8% in real terms in 2025 before falling back to an annualised -6.3% in the first seven months of 2026; disinflation has therefore not by itself repaired real profitability. Second, what drives profitability is not the level of the policy rate but the direction and speed of its change: because liabilities reprice faster than assets, easing cycles widen margins through a repricing gain that is exhausted once rates are held constant. The 86 basis point decline in the gross net interest margin and the 230 basis point compression of the TL loan-deposit spread in April 2026 are a direct observation of this mechanism. Third, and as the paper's principal original contribution, where quantity constraints bind, the interest rate channel is second-order for credit growth: the 2% eight-week growth ceiling set for non-SME Turkish lira loans in May 2026 implies an annual nominal ceiling of 13.7%, i.e. a real contraction of roughly 13.5% at current inflation. Realised credit growth, at an annualised 34.2%, nonetheless substantially exceeds these ceilings. The paper conceptualises this gap as a regulatory wedge and attributes it to leakage arising from exemption scope, segment composition and exchange rate effects. The findings indicate that modelling transmission in Türkiye through a single price variable is misleading, and that regulatory quantity constraints must be explicitly internalised.

title: AI Labels and Offering Size: A Hedonic Analysis of the SEC Form D Census, 2021-2026

detail.abstract: Between 2021 and 2026 the artificial intelligence investment cycle reshaped venture capital, but whether AI labels command higher start-up offering sizes remains contested. Using the SEC Form D regulatory record across nine non-consecutive quarters (2021Q2-2026Q1; 130,057 deduplicated filings and 71,702 declared offerings above USD 10,000), we estimate hedonic offering-size regressions. The corrected specification does not confirm a positive post-2022 AI premium and does not rule out small-to-moderate premiums: the AI × post-2022 interaction is-0.0029 (robust standard error 0.1740; 95% confidence interval-0.344 to +0.338; p = 0.9867), and none of five specifications is positive and significant. The apparent divergence is a right-tail phenomenon: in 2026 the mean AI offering is 2.31× the non-AI mean (bootstrap 95% confidence interval 0.25-7.94, including 1), while an exploratory rank-shift test is significant (p = 0.018, sensitive to classifier breadth); the median AI offering is smaller (0.70×) and the mean ratio falls to 0.93× under 1/99 winsorization. Overall top-1% capital concentration fell from 92.88% in 2021 to 59.11% in 2026 even as the largest AI rounds grew. We read the cycle as capital intensity plus extreme right-tail concentration in a few frontier financings, not a broad-based AI premium.

detail.abstract: A parent that lends to its subsidiary at no interest usually records the loan at face value in its own accounts. A tax authority can price the same loan at a market rate. This paper measures the difference between the two, which it calls the gap, and identifies what drives it. It reads the parent-only accounts of four listed entities in Malaysia, Singapore and Sweden. It takes market rates from three loan rulings in Italy, India and Germany. It then runs a transparent Excel model across four rate cases. Three routes explain why a parent books no interest: loans repayable on demand, net-investment treatment, and a local exemption in Sweden. For DNeX’s RM377.9m interest-free balance, the yearly gap is RM14.5m to RM20.1m at rates of 3.83% to 5.32%. At a 4.9% government bond benchmark it is RM18.5m. For Wasco’s RM7.7m it is RM0.29m to RM0.41m. The accounting route matters more than the rate. Treating the same loan as a term loan under IFRS 9 B5.1.1 cuts the year-one gap by RM13.2m. Moving across the full rate range changes it by RM5.6m. IFRS 9 values the instrument and does not price the support, so the gap is mainly a disclosure matter. The paper describes how the gap arises. It does not estimate how common it is.

detail.abstract: This article reformulates the Meta-Structural Regenerative Model of Existential Exhaustion (MSRM-EE) through the philosophy of Finite Continuance. The central proposition is that existential exhaustion should be understood as a process in which the capacities that enable a finite subject to continue through change become progressively eroded. These capacities include bodily regulation, temporal openness, relational differentiation, symbolic flexibility, desire, practical agency, and the ability to reorganize one's life when existing arrangements cease to be viable. Finite Continuance provides the ontological framework for interpreting these dimensions as interdependent capacities within an erosive field. A subject persists through provisional stabilization, constitutive exchange, and continuing reconfiguration. Continuance therefore depends on more than the maintenance of a current identity or the endurance of present functioning. It also depends on preserving the capacity to alter one's organization and to retain the conditions under which further configurations remain possible. The revised model distinguishes ordinary fatigue, clinical syndromes, existential distress, and structural exhaustion while recognizing their possible interaction. It identifies six mechanisms of erosion: temporal foreclosure, uncontrolled permeability, sedimentation of erosive relations, depletion of desire and initiative, symbolic narrowing, and extractive performance regimes. It then develops a regenerative architecture organized around interruption, sufficient stabilization, regulated permeability, embodied rhythm, reopening of future agency, reconfiguration of desire and interpretation, reciprocal relationality, and institutional responsibility. The model introduces the Threshold of Sufficiency as a way to identify when available resources and conditions fall below what is required to preserve basic reconfigurative capacity. It also treats recovery as the restoration of capacities and enabling conditions rather than a demand for rapid optimization. The paper presents eight testable hypotheses and a research agenda while distinguishing philosophical claims from empirical propositions. MSRM-EE is offered as a theoretical framework for investigation, not as a validated clinical instrument or treatment protocol. Its principal contribution is to connect existential exhaustion with the erosion of future agency and to make the preservation of reconfigurative capacity a central concern of philosophical psychology and institutional ethics.

detail.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in knowledge-intensive organisations, most attention has gone to its productivity gains. Less has gone to what continuous reliance on these tools does to an organisation's epistemic health: its capacity to evaluate claims, use local knowledge and develop expertise. A correct output, a complete decision record and the formal presence of a human reviewer do not, on their own, show that people have evaluated the knowledge they act on. Drawing on Nonaka's SECI model, cognitive offloading theory, research on automation bias and accounts of epistemic agency, I identify four failure modes of unchecked AI integration: automation bias and overreliance, epistemic atrophy, breakdown of tacit knowledge transmission, and intellectual homogenisation. In response, I propose an Epistemic Audit Framework with four dimensions (Source and Logic Provenance, Contextual Integration, Critical Friction and Reasoning Autonomy), operationalised through a risk-tiered, three-gateway protocol that reintroduces 'desirable friction' where decision stakes justify it, and a three-level rubric that records the quality of evidence on each dimension. Compared with recent frameworks for human oversight and skill preservation, the contribution is integrative: a single, domain-general instrument whose gateways both change decisions and produce the evidence used to assess them. An illustrative vignette and five testable propositions show how the framework could be applied and evaluated. The paper argues that organisations should move from an AI strategy view, which judges AI by efficiency, to an AI knowledge ecology view, which also judges it by how the organisation creates, checks and passes on knowledge.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how financial deepening affects total fertility rates (TFR) through two primary channels: the distribution channel (widening income inequality and rising child-rearing costs) and the industrial structure channel (deindustrialization and shrinking stable employment). Using an unbalanced panel of 80–120 economies from 1980 to 2020, we employ two-way fixed effects models, mediation analysis, and threshold regression to test these mechanisms. Results indicate that financial deepening—measured by private credit to GDP—significantly reduces fertility, with the negative effect concentrated in countries with weak manufacturing sectors and high income inequality. Mechanism tests confirm that declining manufacturing employment and rising Gini coefficients mediate a substantial portion of the total effect. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the fertility-suppressing impact of financial deepening is strongest in East Asian production-type economies and Anglo-Saxon financial-type economies, while social democratic countries with strong redistribution buffers exhibit milder effects. These findings suggest that financial deepening is not inherently detrimental to fertility; rather, its demographic consequences depend critically on the presence of a robust manufacturing base and equitable income distribution. Policy implications emphasize the need to anchor financial development within real economic activities, protect manufacturing employment, and strengthen redistributive mechanisms to stabilize fertility.

detail.abstract: While the individual effects of TFP and FDI on trade flows have been widely studied, their combined influence on bilateral trade remains underexplored. This study examines how TFP and FDI jointly affect India’s bilateral trade with twelve major trading partners over 2015–2023. Country-level TFP is estimated using SFA and incorporated into an augmented gravity model estimated through PPML, accounting for India’s roles as both exporter and importer. The results show that productivity improvements have a stronger effect on exports than imports, with TFP elasticities of 0.71 and 0.43, respectively. FDI promotes both export expansion and import demand, reflecting stronger integration into global value chains. Findings remain robust across alternative productivity measures, fixed-effects structures, and estimation approaches. Overall, the results highlight the importance of productivity-enhancing policies and foreign investment in strengthening India’s trade performance and provide a replicable framework for examining their joint role in bilateral trade.

detail.abstract: Islamic finance has developed from a relatively specialized form of Shariah-compliant intermediation into a diversified international industry spanning Islamic banking, Sukuk, Islamic funds, Takaful, liquiditymanagement instruments, and increasingly digital and sustainability-oriented products. This article asks how that growth, and its institutionalization, has increased the relevance of Islamic finance to development finance in Africa. Using a structured analytical review of academic and institutional sources, this article examines the industry's historical development, the rise of regulatory and standard-setting institutions, the diversification of financial instruments, and the application of Islamic finance to infrastructure, privatesector development, financial inclusion, and sustainability. It argues that asset growth alone poorly measures developmental relevance. What matters is institutionalization: the standards, regulatory arrangements, capital-market infrastructure, and product innovation have created conditions for broader integration with development finance. In Africa, this evolution is particularly relevant to infrastructure financing, long-term capital mobilization, and inclusive growth. Yet, regulatory fragmentation, liquidity constraints, limited market depth, shortages of specialized human capital, and uneven institutional development still constrain the translation of global industry growth into development outcomes. The article concludes that development-finance institutions can contribute most through phased product diversification, strategic partnerships, capacity building, and integration of Islamic finance into their broader developmentfinance strategies.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between financial deepening indicators and total fertility rates (TFR) across 72 economies from 1990 to 2022. While the McKinnonShaw paradigm posits that financial liberalization accelerates economic growth, we argue that it has a “dual face”: improving capital efficiency while potentially suppressing fertility through asset financialization, rising female labor participation, and increased opportunity costs of childrearing. Using an unbalanced panel (N=72, T=33, observations=1,864) and controlling for income, female education, urbanization, social security spending, and infant mortality, we employ twoway fixed effects, IV2SLS (with historical bank density × global financial innovation as instrument), and system GMM to address endogeneity. Results show a robust negative correlation: a 10percentagepoint increase in private sector credittoGDP reduces TFR by 0.31–0.44 children. Heterogeneity analysis reveals the strongest effect in East Asia. Mechanism tests indicate that housing financialization, revaluation of female time, and capitalization of childrearing costs mediate 61% of the total effect. We conclude that the growth benefits of financial deepening may come at the expense of demographic sustainability, calling for integrating fertilitysupportive measures into financial development strategies.

detail.abstract: The dual burden of anaemia and exposure to intimate partner violence (IPV) among ever-married women in India reflects a significant policy crisis in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. This study assesses whether anaemia among women is associated with a greater likelihood of experiencing IPV. Using the National Family Health Survey database and adopting binary logistic regression and different matching methods, we examine the prevalence of anaemia among ever-married women in India and their likely exposure to IPV. The analysis is further extended to a series of sub-sample analyses. Our findings indicate a robust, statistically significant positive association between anaemia and at least one type of IPV (ranging from 1.29 pp to 1.48 pp) among ever-married women. The magnitude is equivalent to around 5% of the average IPV prevalence in the control group. The associations are statistically significant for emotional and physical violence, but not for sexual violence. The results of the sub-sample analysis (across rural and urban areas, poor and non-poor households, education (low and high schooling), castes (reserved versus general category) and sub-samples for the pre-COVID period) reveal compelling heterogeneity for any IPV and individual forms of violence, i.e., emotional and physical, but not for sexual violence.

detail.abstract: In this article, we analyze how popular and trade-oriented news organizations framed coverage of generative AI (genAI) during the first year following the public launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. Journalism plays a crucial role in shaping sociotechnical imaginaries of genAI, therefore influencing development, adoption, investment, and policy, and thus shaping the role the technology ultimately plays in society at large. Through a mixed methods analysis including automated topic modeling and textual analyses, we discovered five key frames in the news corpus, which we call 'Cultural Generativity,' 'Labor,' 'Information Use,' 'Surveillance,' and 'Human Condition.' Ultimately, we criticize the news coverage of genAI as either too narrow and reactive to specific events (such as the Hollywood strike of 2023), or too broad and vague in scope (such as think pieces about the existential meaning of AI), while overlooking crucial meso-level consequences of the technology, including significant financial, political, and environmental risks.

detail.abstract: This paper takes a quasi-experimental differences-indifferences approach to assess the PLI scheme's outcomes in the Auto sector. Namely, we assess sales, raw material cost as a percentage of sales (RMC%), and fixed investment in the form of (log) net block on a hand-matched panel of auto and auto component manufacturers. The most intriguing finding seems to imply that the PLI's outcomes on net block scale with firm size. However, this finding should be seen as suggestive due to a lower significance threshold (bootstrap p = 0.078) owing to a small sample. We situate this finding in the broader context of the structural exclusion of smaller firms from PLI benefits and, indeed, the benefits of India's strong headline growth. We understand the PLI as indicative of an industrial policy of "picking champions," and we contrast it with South Korea's approach to the same. We conclude by making some policy recommendations.

detail.abstract: The paper aims to empirically demonstrate the country-of-origin effects of FDI on wages in the Indian manufacturing sector. We have employed firm-level panel data by mapping FDI and PROWESS data for the time period 2011-12 to 2020-21. Our results show that FDI has a significant positive impact on wages in the Indian manufacturing sector. Furthermore, we find that FDI from the USA has a significant positive impact on average wages. We also find that direct investment coming from tax haven countries (Mauritius, Cayman Islands, and Cyprus) has a positive impact on wages. Our results suggest that the average wage of the Indian manufacturing firms receiving FDI from the USA are significantly higher than the other firms. On the other hand, FDI from Asia and Europe does not have statistically significant impact on wages.

detail.abstract: Shrinkflation means when a product sells with less quantity at the same price.The price of the products stays the same but the price per gram increases. The study shows 23 packaged branded products which were sold in Bangladesh between 2023 and 2026 and analyzes how its pack size ,listed price and effective unit price (EUP) changed at the same period.The data came from an online grocery shop by using archived web pages (2023) and live pages (2026). On average ,the effective unit price (EUP) increased by 10.2% (95% confidence interval : 5.0% to 15.3%) , while the listed price rose by only 4 %.Eight products were shrinkflation cases. Their package sizes decreased by an average of 14.0%, while their listed prices remained unchanged. As a result, their EUP rose by 17.7% on average. All eight were snacks. Another eight products had a direct price rise, averaging 11.5%, while seven products did not change. Shrinkflation was especially common among snacks and bakery items,occurring in 8 of 10 products but it was not observed in any of the 13 other products. The sample is small and was not randomly selected. So, the findings are exploratory and it suggests that listed prices alone can hide part of a real price increase.

detail.abstract: Many decentralized exchanges use automated market makers (AMMs), which execute trades against liquidity pools according to deterministic reserve-based rules. When external prices move, arbitrageurs realign the pool with the market, transferring value from liquidity providers-an adverse-selection cost known as loss-versus-rebalancing (LVR). Milionis et al. (2022a) establish a general LVR identity for such pools. We specialize this identity explicitly to Balancer-style multi-asset automated market makers with a weighted geometric-mean invariant. Deriving the arbitrage-aligned reserves and pool value, we obtain a closed-form pairwise representation: instantaneous LVR equals half the pool value times a weighted sum of pairwise relative-return quadratic variations, so multi-asset LVR is driven by cross-asset return dispersion rather than by marginal variance alone. We derive an exact finite-grid benchmark gap for the Balancer invariant, connect it to covariance-based predictors via a second-order Taylor expansion with an explicit remainder, and show it converges to the continuous-time identity as the observation grid is refined. We validate these theoretical predictions empirically in synthetic multi-asset cryptocurrency pools.

detail.abstract: Mobile health clinics are often justified by their ability to reach populations that fixed facilities miss, but few analyses compare them with the obvious alternative: building a fixed clinic. Building on the AIaugmented mobile unit architecture of Alamu and Onyeama (2026), whose cost claims rest on a simulation, we develop an open probabilistic model comparing one AI-augmented mobile unit with one new fixed clinic in a 2,000 km² zero-access catchment. Fixed-clinic uptake declines with distance, mobile uptake rises with visit frequency and is capped by daily capacity, and outcomes are DALYs averted via diagnosis and treatment. With 29 uncertain inputs drawn 20,000 times at each of several population densities, the median cost per DALY averted at 60 people per km² was $944 for the fixed clinic and $1,612 for the mobile unit.

detail.abstract: General-purpose technologies create large opportunities but make their distribution across firms difficult to assess in real time. We use banks as interpreters of the rise of generative AI by studying lender-specific probability-of-default (PD) estimates for private firms in four large euro-area economies. As public attention to AI rises after ChatGPT, banks lower assessed default risk for borrowers in highly AI-exposed industries by about 5%. The reassessment is weaker for labor-intensive firms and stronger among lenders with pre-existing industry expertise. Yet the favorable industry-level effect is accompanied by a systematic reordering within product markets: banks reassess firms with stronger pre-ChatGPT market positions less favorably relative to their competitors, compressing the risk advantage associated with market leadership. Credit allocation moves in the same direction, with market leaders experiencing relatively lower drawn and committed credit, more relationship exits, and fewer new lenders. The reordering also predicts subsequent bad-credit events beyond banks’ consensus PDs. Internal bank assessments therefore provide a forward-looking measure of how generative AI is expected to reshape competitive risk.

detail.title: Regulatory incentives and the structure of euro area money markets
detail.abstract: This paper quantifies the regulatory cost of short-term money market transactions and analyses how post-global financial crisis prudential reforms shape the structure of euro area money markets and the redistribution of central bank reserves. As the stock of reserves declines with the normalisation of the European Central Bank’s balance sheet, trading in money markets is becoming increasingly important to banks’ liquidity management. As the related money market volumes rise, regulatory constraints may become a more visible determinant of trading activity and short-term rate formation. Focusing on key Basel III requirements – the liquidity coverage ratio, net stable funding ratio and leverage ratio – the paper derives stylised estimates of the marginal regulatory cost associated with unsecured and secured interbank transactions. The results indicate that unsecured interbank lending entails material regulatory costs, estimated at around 35 basis points for lenders and around 15 basis points for borrowers in the second half of 2025, reflecting capital and stable funding requirements. By contrast, secured transactions such as repurchase agreements benefit from substantially lower costs, typically well below 10 basis points when backed by high-quality collateral. These differences create structural incentives favouring secured over unsecured intermediation, suggesting that repo markets are likely to remain the main channel for reserve redistribution as the stock of reserves declines. The findings imply that post-crisis regulation has contributed to a persistent shift in the structure of euro area money markets, with implications for liquidity distribution and monetary policy implementation.

detail.abstract: Mortgage constraints are widely used to reduce household leverage, but lower credit volumes alone say little about who bears the cost or whether financial vulnerability falls. We decompose the effect of a mortgage constraint tightening into three components: the direct effect on households, the equilibrium incidence through house prices, rents and credit supply and, finally, the corrective benefit. We use this framework to synthesize householdlevel, housing-market, lender, crosscountry and credit-crisis evidence. The direct effect falls on young and low-wealth households, largely through fewer mortgage originations. Aggregate credit responses are several times larger than mechanically aggregated micro responses, consistent with general equilibrium amplification, although settings and outcomes differ across studies. Quantitative evidence on the corrective benefit is scarce, and few of the 154 tightening episodes we examine occur when credit and house-price growth is high.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces an endogenous network of payment chains into a business-cycle model. Some production orders are paid upfront, while others are settled only after the buyer receives payment from its own customers. When production or fulfillment waits for settlement, liquidity shortages can propagate through the payment network, leave resources idle, and cause a reduction in measured productivity. We bring the model to Costa Rican data linking interbank business payments to the universe of electronic invoices, connecting contractual terms, payment timing, and delivery timing. We identify payment chains: firms that pay suppliers only after being paid by customers. Exploiting an unexpected freeze of buyers' funds, we find evidence of TFP declines associated with payment delays. We then embed payment chains into a business-cycle model where firms decide to rely on chained payments. Liquidity shocks delay transactions, feed back into aggregate productivity, and generate hysteresis and pecuniary externalities.

detail.abstract:
Background: Lung cancer imposes a heavy burden on the NHS, where rising imaging demand and workforce shortages delay early diagnosis. Despite early promise, real-world cost-effectiveness evidence for artificial intelligence (AI) deployment remains limited.

Methods: We evaluated the cost-effectiveness of AI deployment in chest diagnostic imaging versus standard practice for patients referred with potential lung cancer (LC). A short-term decision-tree model evaluated the cost-utility from an NHS and Personal Social Services perspective.Costs and health outcomes were estimated using data from ten NHS England radiology services and published literature, while chest X-ray sensitivity and specificity estimates were derived from a single NHS trust. Cost-effectiveness was assessed using incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, and incremental net monetary benefit (INMBs).

Findings: AI deployment showed no evidence of improved health outcomes versus standard practice (incremental quality-adjusted life years [QALYs], <0.001), but reduced costs by £2.05 per patient. The INMB was positive at thresholds £15,000/QALY (£3.62), £20,000/QALY (£4.14) and £30,000/QALY (£5.19) respectively.Chest X-ray specificity was the main driver of incremental costs and QALYs in sensitivity analyses. AI remained less costly and equally effective in all scenarios assessed including hypothetical autonomous AI reporting of high confidence normal images.

Interpretation: This evaluation provides early, real‑world evidence consistent with AI deployment in chest imaging for suspected LC being cost-effective through modest cost savings rather than health gains. However, the uncontrolled pre-post design limits causal inference, and concurrent system changes may have influenced results. Scenario analyses suggest that autonomous reporting and shared licensing could deliver additional efficiencies and cost savings.
